trust_decision.summary: Whether a client-supplied X-ProxyHost / X-Forwarded-Host value may replace the server host when NiFi builds absolute URLs; at the pinned commit nothing checks it against nifi.web.proxy.host, and the fix adds a check at the Jetty connector for HTTPS requests.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'constructing qualified URLs'. This line picks the URL host from X-ProxyHost/X-Forwarded-Host without an allow-list, and the context-path check right beside it (lines 176-180) shows what a matching host check would look like.

fix_sites.entry_point: NiFi framework HTTPS server startup (constructor reads nifi.web.proxy.host into validProxyHosts, fix.diff:77)
every HTTP request on the framework connector (customizer registered, fix.diff:89-90)
config parsing helper getValidProxyHosts splitting host:port entries (fix.diff:99-110)
new ProxyHeaderValidatorCustomizer.customize, applied to every secure request (REST API, UI, OIDC/SAML, site-to-site, cluster replication)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix is one connector-level guard plus wiring in nifi-jetty. It never touches the URL builders (nifi-commons) or the resources that use them.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: NiFi Registry is a separate application with its own Jetty server and properties. It has no nifi.web.proxy.host equivalent, and it reads X-Forwarded-Server instead of X-Forwarded-Host, so a solver can say the NiFi advisory does not cover it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Several things must keep working: a proxy header equal to the request's own (SNI/SAN-validated) host, allow-listed hosts whose property entry includes a port, plain-HTTP mode which has no check, and cluster request replication, which re-sets X-ProxyHost to the resolved host before forwarding to other nodes. Rejecting every proxy header, or checking HTTP mode too, breaks proxied and clustered deployments.

O6_input_shapes: both headers present (each one checked, not just the first)
empty or blank header value (rejected, while the URI provider skips blanks, StandardRequestUriProvider.java:191)
header equal to the request Host
allow-list entries written as host:port (port removed before comparing)

O7_producer.where: nifi-commons/nifi-properties/src/main/java/org/apache/nifi/util/NiFiProperties.java:1603-1608 (getAllowedHostsAsList); the fix adds host-only parsing at fix.diff:99-110

O8_uncovered_routes.route: NiFi Registry REST resources build entity and Location URIs from X-ProxyHost / X-Forwarded-Server with no allow-list; the Registry connector has no proxy-host customizer
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A separate product with its own server (nifi-registry/nifi-registry-core/nifi-registry-jetty/src/main/java/org/apache/nifi/registry/jetty/connector/ApplicationServerConnectorFactory.java:127-134) and no proxy-host property, so a fix needs a new config key
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different top-level module (nifi-registry vs nifi-framework-bundle/nifi-commons), different header constant set

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Site-to-site peer listing passes every raw request header, X-ProxyHost included, to PeerDescriptionModifier routing expressions without going through StandardRequestUriProvider, so a fix only in the URI provider misses it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This already exists at the pinned commit. Only the connector-level check covers it. It is a how-type test of whether the solver checks at the request layer or only in the URL builder.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A port differential: getPort takes the port from a host:port proxy header, while the published check compares the raw header against host-only values, so an added proxy-port header path (X-ProxyPort/X-Forwarded-Port, line 140) stays unchecked against allowed ports
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Ports are already handled by a separate customizer (HostPortValidatorCustomizer.java:59-78) that only looks at the Host/authority port, not proxy port headers. A maintainer could easily leave them split.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Allow-list parsing differential: splitting entries on ':' (fix.diff:104) mangles IPv6 entries such as [::1]:8443, which the docs say are accepted
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The neighbouring getValidPorts uses a different regex for the same property. Two parsers of one property drift apart.

O9_family: CWE-346 origin validation / Host-header injection into generated absolute URLs (redirects, resource URIs, OIDC/SAML callback URIs)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven (multi-module); only nifi-jetty plus nifi-web-servlet-shared and nifi-properties are needed for this area
O10_build.project_tests: nifi-framework-bundle/nifi-framework/nifi-web/nifi-jetty/src/test/java/org/apache/nifi/web/server/StandardServerProviderTest.java (starts an embedded HTTPS server with an ephemeral keystore, sends requests over loopback); nifi-commons/nifi-web-servlet-shared/src/test/java/org/apache/nifi/web/servlet/shared/StandardRequestUriProviderTest.java

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a host allow-list in StandardRequestUriProvider.getHost (falling back to the server name), copying the context-path check. This misses site-to-site raw-header routing and NiFi Registry, and silently ignores the header instead of returning 421.

out_of_scope_notes: NiFi Registry ApplicationResource.getBaseUri also takes X-ProxyContextPath/X-Forwarded-Context and port headers without an allow-list (nifi-registry/nifi-registry-core/nifi-registry-web-api/src/main/java/org/apache/nifi/registry/web/api/ApplicationResource.java:92-107); that is a context-path issue, not followed up.
unverified: Whether the published check breaks cluster replication: ApplicationResource.java:332 sets X-ProxyHost to the resolved host before forwarding to other nodes, and the receiving node rejects it unless it is in nifi.web.proxy.host. Not traced through the replicator.
